hints: Expand the brackets on the right-hand side.
Collect the $\sin 2x$ terms on one side and $\cos 2x$ terms on the other.
walkthrough:
Expand the right-hand side of the trigonometric equation:
$$\sin 2x + 3\cos 2x = 3\sin 2x - 3\cos 2x$$

Group $\sin 2x$ terms on one side and $\cos 2x$ terms on the other:
$$3\cos 2x + 3\cos 2x = 3\sin 2x - \sin 2x \implies 6\cos 2x = 2\sin 2x$$

Divide by $\cos 2x$ and by $2$ to express the equation in terms of $\tan 2x$:
$$\frac{\sin 2x}{\cos 2x} = \frac{6}{2} \implies \tan 2x = 3$$

hints: Note that the range for $2x$ is $-180^\circ \le 2x \le 180^\circ$.
Find the two values of $2x$ that satisfy $\tan 2x = 3$ in this interval.
Divide by $2$ to obtain $x$ to $1$ decimal place.
walkthrough:
Find the principal solution for $2x$ using inverse tangent with the transformed interval $-180^\circ \le 2x \le 180^\circ$:
$$2x = \tan^{-1}(3) \approx 71.57^\circ$$

Find the second solution in the interval by subtracting $180^\circ$:
$$2x = 71.57^\circ - 180^\circ = -108.43^\circ$$

Divide each value of $2x$ by $2$ to obtain the solutions for $x$:
$$x = \frac{71.57^\circ}{2} \approx 35.8^\circ$$
$$x = \frac{-108.43^\circ}{2} \approx -54.2^\circ$$
